This also gives the psychological theorist the resources to resist the Teletransportation Argument. On this kind of view, premises (1) and (2) are false, because the psychological connections to Marsy and Venusy are branching connections.

The puzzle here is only superficial. Roads are things which have different spatial parts located in difference places. Two roads can occupy the same space just by sharing some of the same parts. No big deal.
There are also (as the contemporary philosopher Mark Johnston points out) practical problems.
But of course we can also select smaller collections of temporal parts. Consider the collection that starts the day after mid semester break and ends the last day of exams.

One can describe this situation in a way which makes it seem mysterious. I-90 and I-94 are separate highways; the stretch of highway north of 65th street is one highway; and yet it is identical to both I-90 and I-94. How can this be???
You think that you know that you are the person you remember being. But, if that other body survives to become a living person, you will not be the person you remember being.
This is a strange and surprising view. Here is one way to get your mind around it. Consider a case in which two roads ‘overlap’ in space.
You survive as both A and B.
But this looks bad for the psychological theory; after all, you seem to have the right kinds of connections to both A and B.

My Division. My body is fatally injured, as are the brains of my two brothers. My brain is divided, and each half is successfully transplanted into the body of one of my brothers. Each of the resulting people believes that he is me, seems to remember living my life, has my character, and is in every other way psychologically continuous with me. And he has a body that is very like mine.
Notice that a materialist could say much the same thing. They could say that what is required for your survival is a non-branching material relation to some future thing.

We rejected this on the grounds that Lefty is not identical to Righty, so that you cannot be identical to both. But this neglects a possibility: maybe you were already Lefty and Righty. You thought that you were one person; but in fact you were already two.
You survive as Lefty and Righty.

On one view, people -- and other objects -- have a relation to time which is similar to the relation in which roads stand to space. Like roads, we seem to have spatial parts. But no this view, we also have temporal parts. Just as I exist in separate locations by having separate spatial parts in those distinct locations, so I exist at different times by having different temporal parts in those different times.
Suppose that these are all of your temporal parts. (In fact, there would be vastly more.) On the four-dimensionalist view, you are identical to this large collection of temporal parts.
Here’s a quite different way of responding to My Division. Recall this option:

That is not you; it is only part of you. But it still exists: it is a collection of psychologically related temporal parts. Let’s call (following Johnston) this sort of ‘part of a person’ a ‘personite.’
